arxiv-2302-09186.title: Shallow current of viscous fluid flowing between diverging or converging walls
arxiv-2302-09186.creator: M-S. Liu 1 , 2, H. E. Huppert 3 , 4
arxiv-2302-09186.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M-S. Liu 1 , 2, H. E. Huppert 3 , 4. We investigate the shallow flow of viscous fluid into and out of a channel whose gap width increases as a power-law ( x n x^{n} ), where x x is the downstream axis. The fluid flows slowly, while injected at a rate in the form of t α t^{\alpha} , where t t is time and α \alpha is a constant.

arxiv-2312-02081.title: Copula-based deviation measure of cointegrated financial assets
arxiv-2312-02081.description: Abstract This study outlines a comprehensive methodology utilizing copulas to discern inconsistencies in the behavior exhibited by pairs of financial assets. It introduces a robust approach to establishing the interrelationship between the returns of these assets, exploring potential measures of dependence among the stochastic variables represented by these returns.

arxiv-2404-14035.title: A stochastic population model with hierarchic size-structure
arxiv-2404-14035.creator: Carles Barril, Àngel Calsina, József Z. Farkas
arxiv-2404-14035.description: Abstract We consider a hierarchically structured population in which the amount of resources an individual has access to is affected by individuals that are larger, and that the intake of resources by an individual only affects directly the growth rate of the individual.

arxiv-2602-05020.title: Decaying Sensitivity of the Zero Solution for a Class of Nonlinear Optimal Control Problems The authors thank Andrii Mironchenko, Manuel Schaller, and Karl Worthmann for valuable discussions and helpful comments. This work was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Found
arxiv-2602-05020.creator: Lars Grüne, Mario Sperl
arxiv-2602-05020.description: Abstract We study spatial decay properties of sensitivities in a nonlinear optimal control problem with a graph-structured interaction topology. For a problem with nonlinear decoupled dynamics and quadratic cost, we show that a localized perturbation of the zero reference leads to an optimal trajectory that decays exponentially with the graph distance.

pmc-10572818.title: Forensic Proteomics for the Discovery of New post mortem Interval Biomarkers: A Preliminary Study
pmc-10572818.creator: Alessandro Marrone, Daniele La Russa, Laura Barberio, Maria Stella Murfuni, Marco Gaspari, Daniela Pellegrino, Francesco Sessa, Monica Salerno
pmc-10572818.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Estimating the time since death (post mortem interval, PMI) represents one of the most important tasks in daily forensic casework. For decades, forensic scientists have investigated changes in post mortem body composition, focusing on different physical, chemical, or biological aspects, to discover a reliable method for estimating PMI; nevertheless, all of these attempts remain unsuccessful considering the currently available methodical spectrum characterized by great inaccuracies and limitations. However, recent promising approaches focus on the post mortem decomposition of biomolecules.

pmc-11615699.creator: Isaac Isiko, Kelly Taremwa, Simon Nyegenye, Aaron Mwesigwa, Reagan Muwanga Mutebi, Lenz Nwachinemere Okoro, Eneh Nchiek Edet, Catherine Chepkoskei Koech, Naya Gadzama Bulus, Jackson Micheal Asingwire
pmc-11615699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThis study aimed to determine the factors associated with feeling ashamed of disclosing HIV‐positive status among females who self‐reported to health facilities for HIV testing in Kenya.MethodThis study used the Kenya Demographic Health Survey data set for 2022. pmc-13447498.title: Supplementary Motor Area Meningioma and Postoperative Hemorrhage Presenting With Acquired Narcissistic Personality Traits: A Case Report
pmc-13447498.creator: So Jin Kwak, Sangwoo Kim, Dae Hyun Kim, Won Hyuk Chang
pmc-13447498.description: Meningiomas involving the supplementary motor area (SMA) are known to cause motor deficits, but acquired narcissistic personality changes following such lesions rarely described. We report a rare case of a 63-year-old woman who developed acquired narcissistic personality traits following the resection of a right frontal parasagittal meningioma involving the SMA, complicated by postoperative hemorrhage.
